summary: Round 1 (new module). Both rows are unmarked and correctly partial. Déf. 2 (`IsCompatibleAssoc σ f`, `IsCompatible f`) is the printed definition for p = 2 and factors of one dimension a: f · [m₁, m₂] = torus(μ) · [φ₁ m_{σ(1)}, φ₂ m_{σ(2)}] with φᵢ : F(B_{σ(i)}) ≃ₜ F(Bᵢ) conical, the order of indices exactly « m'ᵢ = φᵢ m_{σ(i)} » (for the transposition φ₁ : F(B₂) → F(B₁) applied to m₂), and « f ∈ {F⁻¹(φ)} × (ℝ^{+p}/ℝ^+) » read as composition with a torus element. Prop. 4's two assertions are proved for p = 2, same dimension, nonempty factors (`homogeneous_of_compatible`: the composite along the cycle of 1, h = 2; `balayable_of_compatible`: the index-≤ p! argument made concrete with one transposition-type pair of isomorphisms). The hypotheses read « le groupe des automorphismes compatibles » as the SET of compatible automorphisms; this is equivalent to the printed group only once the set is shown closed under composition and inverse, which is true for p = 2 but not proved (minor). [Nonempty Bᵢ] is genuinely needed (an empty factor empties the product and makes both hypotheses vacuous) and is an « added » reading needing a ruling. No issue against what is proved; ready to graduate as partial.

checks.def2: IsCompatibleAssoc (σ : Perm (Fin 2)) f := (σ = 1 ∧ ∃ φ₁ : F(B₁) ≃ₜ F(B₁), φ₂ : F(B₂) ≃ₜ F(B₂), conical, ∃ μ, ∀ x, f·mk x = torusMap μ (mk (φ₁ x₁, φ₂ x₂))) ∨ (σ = swap 0 1 ∧ ∃ φ₁ : F(B₂) ≃ₜ F(B₁), φ₂ : F(B₁) ≃ₜ F(B₂), conical, ∃ μ, ∀ x, f·mk x = torusMap μ (mk (φ₁ x₂, φ₂ x₁))). Matches « un système {φᵢ} de p isomorphismes coniques affins entre F(B_{σ(i)}) et F(Bᵢ) … m'ᵢ = φᵢ m_{σ(i)} … f ∈ {F⁻¹(φ)} × (R^{+p}/R^+) » and « associé à la permutation σ ». torusMap ranges over all of ℝ₊*²/ℝ₊* (class of (1, μ)). The inverse of a conical homeomorphism is conical (IsGXMorphism.homeomorph_symm), so ≃ₜ + forward morphism is « isomorphisme conique ». `perm_fin_two` (decide) makes the two disjuncts exhaustive. The same-dimension restriction: a conical isomorphism F(B_{σ(i)}) ≅ F(Bᵢ) forces equal dimensions, so for p = 2 with a ≠ b only σ = id occurs — a reading, correctly not called a finding

Symmetric for B₂. balayable_of_compatible: K₁ = pr₁(K), K₂ = pr₂(K); if some pair of projective isomorphisms t₁ : B₂ ≅ B₁, t₂ : B₁ ≅ B₂ exists, K₁ ∪ t₂⁻¹(K₂) is a generating domain for B₁ (a transposition-type f contributes θ₁ ∘ t₂ applied to t₂⁻¹(k₂)), else every compatible f is identity-type and K₁ suffices — the content of « G_I d'indice fini ≤ p! », made concrete. Both correct

issues.problem: The SCOPE says the group structure is « the printed proof's device, not its conclusion ». But Prop. 4's HYPOTHESES are stated for « le groupe des automorphismes compatibles »; the Lean hypotheses quantify over the set of compatible automorphisms. If that set were not closed under composition, « the group (generated) acts transitively / sweeps » would be WEAKER than the Lean hypothesis and the formal theorem weaker than the printed one. The set is in fact a group for p = 2 (closure under composition and inverse: F⁻¹(φ) commutes with the torus up to μ ↦ μ^{±1}), so nothing is wrong — but it is unproved, and it is exactly what makes the formal hypotheses the printed ones
